summary: Iteration 47 - Italian (IT) language support. Backend: 6/6 pytest passed (POST /api/translate target=it returns traditional Italian for Sign of the Cross / Padre nostro / Gloria al Padre; cache hit <5s; target=en passthrough; anon rejected; GET /api/liturgy/lauds/saturday with Accept-Language: it returns Italian liturgy text; EN default does not leak Italian). Frontend (mobile 390x844): Home language toggle correctly shows three chips (lang-en / lang-es / lang-it). Tapping 'Italiano' switches all home strings to Italian (verified: 'Preghiera', 'Bibbia', 'Orario · Il tuo ritmo di preghiera e pratica', 'Nel Mondo · La vita pubblica alla luce della Chiesa'). Switching to ES still works ('Oración', 'En el Mundo'). Switching back to EN restores English. Liturgy of the Hours → Lauds renders Italian end-to-end after ~5-30s (verified markers: 'O Dio, vieni in mio aiuto', 'Gloria al Padre', 'Salmo', 'Cantico', plus translated body 'Le Lodi sono l\'Ora mattutina dell\'Ufficio Divino…'). Prayer / Rosary / Chaplets initially did NOT translate to Italian because frontend src/api.ts:translateTexts() early-returned for any target ≠ 'es'. APPLIED 1-LINE FIX: allow target=='it' as well. After fix verified: Rosary shows 'Santo Rosario / Segno della Croce / Nel nome del Padre e del Figlio e dello Spirito Santo. Amen.' and St Michael Chaplet shows 'Corona di San Michele / Segno della Croce / Nel nome del Padre…'. Remaining minor i18n gap: hardcoded ES/EN ternaries in /app/frontend/app/prayer/[kind].tsx (lines 75-84) for accessory UI strings — 'Bead i of n', 'Prev', 'Next Bead', 'Amen — Continue', 'Journal this', 'Good work for today' — stay in English when IT is active. Prayer hub index (/prayer) hero/blurb/chaplet card titles/subtitles are also hardcoded English (no useTranslator). Daily Devotion card on home (Anima Christi / Morning Offering / Glory Be) is hardcoded English on the home screen.

ui_bugs.issue: FIXED in this iteration: api.ts line 1823 early-returned untranslated text for any target ≠ 'es', so /prayer/* screens never received Italian. Changed condition to `target !== 'es' && target !== 'it'`. Reference: /app/frontend/src/api.ts:1822-1826.

issues: Accessory UI strings ('Bead i of n', 'Prev', 'Next Bead', 'Amen — Continue', 'Amen — Done', 'Journal this', 'Good work for today', 'Buena obra para hoy') only have EN/ES branches via `es ? ... : ...` ternaries (lines 75-84). When IT is active these fall back to English. Should be migrated to t() with IT entries in i18n.tsx, or extend ternaries to include `it` branch.
Mystery selector chips (Joyful/Sorrowful/Glorious/Luminous) on Rosary are hardcoded English literals.

Hero strings ('Anchor the day in prayer', 'Choose the Rosary or a chaplet…'), section labels ('ORATIO', 'TODAY', '~XX min'), and chaplet card titles + subtitles are hardcoded English. None of these go through useTranslator. With IT (or ES) selected the entire prayer hub still reads in English. The user-visible bug from this iteration's user story ('open Preghiera section') therefore renders an English hub then Italian content inside. Consider piping these strings through useTranslator(arr) at the hub level.

DEVOTIONS array (Morning Offering / Glory Be / Anima Christi) in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx is hardcoded English and never passed through useTranslator, so it stays English in both ES and IT. Pre-existing minor gap (not introduced by this iteration).

action_items: MEDIUM: in /app/frontend/app/prayer/[kind].tsx lines 75-84, extend the `es ? a : b` ternaries to handle IT, or move these strings into i18n.tsx t() lookups. Otherwise IT users see Italian prayer body but English navigation controls.
MEDIUM: pipe the Prayer Hub (/app/frontend/app/prayer/index.tsx) hero copy, chaplet titles, and subtitles through useTranslator so the hub itself reads in IT/ES when those langs are active.
LOW: optionally translate the home Daily Devotion card (DEVOTIONS array in /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/index.tsx) via useTranslator for consistency.
OPTIONAL: clean up unused export `translateTexts` parameter validation — current shape is fine but could use the SUPPORTED set from i18n.tsx in the future.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend lang_ctx.resolve_lang correctly maps any Accept-Language starting with 'it' to 'it' and falls back to 'en' — robust.
i18n_translate.SUPPORTED set + _LANG_NAMES mapping is clean; adding new languages is a 2-line change.
Backend translation is cached per (text, target) sha1 in db.translations_cache — second-call latency is sub-100ms, confirmed in test_translate_cache_hit_is_fast.
Frontend i18n.tsx Lang type already includes 'it' and AsyncStorage check accepts it — provider plumbing is sound.
The bug fix in api.ts:translateTexts is the canonical place to add language support, but consider centralizing the supported-target set (currently duplicated as inline check).

No other state created. translations_cache will accumulate Italian rows for tested prayers / Lauds Saturday — these are intentional caches and safe to keep.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Italian translation now works end-to-end. Backend translate accepts target='it'; frontend translateTexts() was patched to call the endpoint for IT (was previously a no-op for any non-ES target). When testing UI, force a chip tap (page.click('[data-testid=lang-it]')) rather than relying solely on localStorage seeding — the JSON-stringified AsyncStorage shim works on reload, but a tap also exercises setLang() and is more reliable. Live liturgy translation takes ~5-30s on first open; chaplet/rosary takes ~15-25s for first open then cached. Note three known i18n gaps (still EN under IT): Prayer hub screen titles/blurbs/chaplet cards, prayer detail nav controls ('Prev'/'Next Bead'/'Bead i of n'), and home Daily Devotion card — see action_items.
rca_of_issue: RCA: /app/frontend/src/api.ts:1823 had `if (target !== 'es' || texts.length === 0) return texts;` which short-circuited any non-Spanish translation request, returning the original English strings. The /api/translate backend supported 'it' all along, but the frontend never sent the request when lang was 'it'. The Liturgy of the Hours pages worked because they fetch /api/liturgy/{hour}/{day} directly with the active Accept-Language header (server-side translation), bypassing the broken helper. Fix: extend the guard to also allow 'it'. Verified by re-running UI tests post-fix — Rosary and St Michael chaplet rendered fully in traditional Italian liturgical text.
